final_answer: Ice floats on water due to the unique molecular structure of water. When water freezes, its molecules form a hexagonal crystalline lattice held together by hydrogen bonds. This arrangement creates open spaces between molecules, making ice less dense than liquid water. Since density determines buoyancy, the lower density of ice allows it to float. This phenomenon is unusual because most substances become denser when solidifying, but water's hydrogen bonding causes this exception.
